# The grid post's invented 300 ms sort reads as a measurement

## Context

The published post `learn/blog/a-data-grid-in-a-web-worker.md` (`#20184`, merged in PR `#20186`) says on line 54:

> If the App Worker spends 300 ms sorting, nothing on the main thread waits for it.

The 300 ms was never measured. It was written to illustrate work that does not block the page. Reader feedback, relayed by the operator on 1 Nov 2026, read it as a measured cost: Neo.mjs's grid needs 300 ms just to sort. It was also the last line many readers reached.

## The Problem

An illustrative number in a public artifact is read as a measured claim about the product it describes. The rest of the post measures its timings and links each one to the benchmark report or the release notes. This one sentence has the same shape and no source. It hands a skeptical reader a cost the grid never showed.

## The Architectural Reality

- The sentence is at `learn/blog/a-data-grid-in-a-web-worker.md:54`, the only occurrence in the repository (`git grep` on `origin/dev`).
- The post's portal registration in `apps/portal/resources/data/blog.json` does not carry the sentence, so the registry needs no change. The generated SEO surfaces (`sitemap.xml`, `llms.txt`) list routes, not this text.
- Every other figure in the post is either sourced (the benchmark report pinned at `4300c48`, the 10.5 and 13.2 release notes) or illustrates no cost of Neo.mjs. An example is the "move this row down 500 pixels" instruction, which shows what a change message looks like.

## The Fix

State the mechanism instead of a number:

> However long the App Worker spends sorting, nothing on the main thread waits for it.

The rest of the paragraph stays as it is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Line 54 states the mechanism and carries no number.
- [ ] No other sentence in the post illustrates a cost of Neo.mjs with an unmeasured number. A list of the post's figures and their sources is in the PR.
- [ ] Post-merge: the deployed post at `https://neomjs.com/news/blog/a-data-grid-in-a-web-worker` shows the new sentence.

## Out of Scope

- Copies of the post outside this repository, such as the Medium publication. The same one-line change applies there, and those surfaces belong to the operator.
- Any rewrite of the post beyond this sentence.

## Related

- `#20184` (the post), PR `#20186` (its merge).
